answers.primary: A subagent: delegate the run to a subagent (ad hoc general-purpose, or a custom test-runner agent file with tools: Bash, Read, Grep if you will repeat it) whose task prompt says to run the suite and report only failing tests with their error messages. This is the documented pattern for isolating high-volume operations: the thousands of log lines live in the subagent's own context window and only its final summary returns.
answers.rejected_alternative: A dynamic workflow, rejected because a single test run is one delegated task, not an orchestration of dozens of agents, and a workflow adds a script plus a plan-approval gate for no isolation benefit that the subagent does not already give.
answers.enforcement_owner: The model. The harness guarantees only that the subagent gets a separate context window and that its intermediate tool output does not enter yours; what the summary contains, and whether it really trims to failures, is the subagent's judgment.
answers.context_boundary: The suite executes in the subagent's context window, which starts fresh with its own system prompt, the delegation message, CLAUDE.md and git status. Only the final report crosses back into your conversation; the raw stdout stays in the subagent transcript file and is deleted after cleanupPeriodDays.
answers.lifecycle: Runs when Claude delegates on your request or the custom agent's description matches; it ends when the subagent returns its summary. Each invocation is a fresh instance, so nothing carries to the next run unless Claude resumes that agent by ID with SendMessage.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open and is advisory: a subagent that pastes back hundreds of lines of raw output re-pollutes exactly the context you were protecting, and a chatty summary of a large failure set can be as expensive as the logs. Background subagents also return their result as a later completion notification, so Claude may report the run as still in progress if you ask too early.
answers.version_caveat: As of v2.1.198 subagents run in the background by default with a narrower built-in tool set that still includes Bash, Read and Grep, so a test runner is unaffected; v2.1.211 makes background results arrive as a completion notification. The 200 subagents per session cap (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION, v2.1.212 or later) applies to repeated runs.

answers.primary: A custom project subagent in .claude/agents/ whose frontmatter sets an explicit allowlist, tools: Read, Grep, Glob, and omits Bash, Write, Edit and Agent. The tool pool is resolved by Claude Code when the subagent is spawned, so no instruction in the body and no mid-task decision by the model can add a mutating tool back.
answers.rejected_alternative: A permissions.deny rule for Edit and Write in settings.json, rejected because deny rules are session-wide: they would also stop the main conversation and every other subagent from editing, rather than constraining just this reviewer.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. Tool filtering happens in Claude Code at spawn time, and the doc is explicit that permission and tool rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model.
answers.context_boundary: The reviewer runs in its own fresh context window with its own system prompt, CLAUDE.md and git status; it never sees your conversation history. Only its written review crosses back, and that report is passed through subagent output scanning before Claude reads it.
answers.lifecycle: Applies for the life of each spawned instance, from the Agent tool call or @-mention until the review is returned; the restriction is a property of the definition, so it re-applies identically on every invocation and on resume.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on tools, but the guarantee is only as tight as the allowlist: leaving Bash in the list would reopen writes through shell redirection, and leaving Agent in would let it spawn a less restricted child. If every entry in the list resolves to nothing the agent refuses to launch with an error rather than starting toolless.
answers.version_caveat: Since v2.1.208 an unresolvable tools list fails the spawn with a named error instead of launching a zero-tool agent. If you ship this reviewer inside a plugin, the hooks, mcpServers and permissionMode fields are ignored, so keep the guarantee in the tools allowlist, which plugin agents do honor.

answers.primary: No extension mechanism: the built-in /btw side question. It answers from the conversation as it already stands, appears in a dismissible overlay, and neither the question nor the answer is written into the transcript.
answers.rejected_alternative: A forked subagent started with /subtask, rejected because a fork also inherits the whole conversation but spends a real agent run and returns its result as a message that does enter your history, which is the one thing you asked to avoid.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code runs the side question out of band against the parent context and discards it; there is no instruction the model could follow or ignore that would change whether it lands in history.
answers.context_boundary: It runs against the full current conversation and reuses the parent prompt cache, so cost is minimal, but it is deliberately tool-free: no file reads, no commands, no search. Nothing crosses back into the conversation; the answer stays in the overlay until dismissed.
answers.lifecycle: Fires when you type /btw with a question, including while Claude is mid-turn, and produces exactly one response with no follow-up turns. It stops applying when you dismiss the overlay; press f to promote the exchange into a new session if you want to continue with tools.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory in the sense that it cannot fail safe or unsafe, it simply cannot act: if the answer needs something not already in context the reply will be a guess or a refusal rather than a lookup. Because it never enters history, the main conversation cannot later refer back to what the side question established.
answers.version_caveat: Running /btw with no question to reopen the overlay requires v2.1.212 or later, and stepping between earlier answers with Left and Right requires v2.1.187. Forking the exchange with f is available in local sessions only.

answers.primary: A forked subagent started with /subtask, for example "/subtask draft regression tests for the bug we just characterized". A fork inherits the entire conversation so far, including every finding, ruled-out hypothesis, config quirk and stack trace, so there is nothing to re-explain, and it runs in the background while you keep debugging.
answers.rejected_alternative: A named custom test-writer subagent, rejected because a non-fork subagent starts with a fresh context window and would only get whatever Claude compresses into the delegation message, which is exactly the two hours of accumulated findings you do not want summarized away.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness owns the context inheritance and the isolation; the model owns whether the drafted tests are any good. Claude Code copies the parent history, system prompt, tools and model into the fork and keeps the fork's tool calls out of your window.
answers.context_boundary: The fork gets the full conversation as of the moment it spawns, plus the same system prompt and tool pool, and shares the parent prompt cache. Its own tool calls and file reads stay in the fork; only its final result crosses back as a message in your conversation.
answers.lifecycle: Starts when you run /subtask and runs in the background until it returns, or until you stop it with x in the panel below the prompt. It is a snapshot: findings you and Claude produce after the fork spawns never reach it unless you open its transcript and message it.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open. The fork has your full tool pool, so it can edit files while you edit the same files, and its edits land in your checkout unless it was spawned with isolation: worktree. It also cannot spawn further forks, and it consumes the session subagent budget like any other agent.
answers.version_caveat: /subtask requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later; on v2.1.161 through v2.1.211 the command is /fork, and before v2.1.161 it needed CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1. Claude spawning forks on its own is still experimental and may change; set CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT to 1 or 0 to force the behavior regardless of the staged rollout.

answers.primary: A skill invoked by name with context: fork and agent: Explore in its frontmatter, so the written procedure becomes the prompt that drives a read-only forked subagent, plus allowed-tools such as Bash(gh *) for the read-only CLI calls the steps need. Add disable-model-invocation: true if it should only ever run when a person types its name.
answers.rejected_alternative: A plain skill running in the main conversation, rejected because a non-forked skill's file reads and command output all land in the invoking context window, which is the specific outcome the team wants to avoid.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split, and worth being precise: the harness owns both the isolation (the fork gets its own context) and the read-only capability (Explore denies Write and Edit). The model owns only whether it follows the written steps in order.
answers.context_boundary: The forked subagent starts from the skill content as its task and the Explore system prompt, with no conversation history; because the agent is Explore it also skips CLAUDE.md and git status. Only the final summary returns to the invoking session; every intermediate read and command output stays in the fork.
answers.lifecycle: Fires when a team member types the skill name; the skill's rendered content becomes the fork's prompt and the run ends when the subagent returns. As of v2.1.218 the fork runs in the background so the invoking session stays free; set background: false to block the invoking turn instead.
answers.failure_mode: Isolation and read-only fail closed, procedure adherence fails open: nothing forces the agent through the steps, and a skill written as guidelines rather than an actionable task returns nothing useful from a fork. A backgrounded fork also gets the narrower background tool set, so a step depending on a tool outside it silently has no way to run.
answers.version_caveat: Background execution for forked skills requires v2.1.218; earlier versions always blocked the invoking turn. If the procedure relies on inline !`command` context injection, the managed setting disableSkillShellExecution replaces those commands with a placeholder, and ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} substitution inside allowed-tools needs v2.1.129 or later.

answers.primary: The worker's subagent definition should list the guide in its skills frontmatter field, for example skills: [api-conventions]. That injects the full skill content into the subagent's context at startup rather than leaving it to be discovered, which is the documented difference between preloaded and discoverable.
answers.rejected_alternative: Naming the conventions in the subagent's system prompt body and telling it to invoke the skill through the Skill tool, rejected because that keeps the guidance merely discoverable: the model decides whether to load it, which is exactly the behavior that is failing today.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split by layer: the harness guarantees the text is present at startup, the model owns compliance with it. Preloading removes the discovery failure but cannot make the worker obey the conventions.
answers.context_boundary: The subagent runs in its own fresh context window; the skill's full content, the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and git status load at startup, but the main conversation's history and the skills you invoked there do not cross the boundary. Only the worker's result comes back.
answers.lifecycle: Injected at spawn, every time this subagent type is spawned, and present for the whole of that instance's run; it does not persist to the next invocation except that resuming the same agent keeps its existing context.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open on the outcome and, worse, quietly: if the named skill is missing, disabled, or sets disable-model-invocation: true, Claude Code skips it and only logs a warning to the debug log, so the worker launches without the conventions and looks the same from outside. Large preloaded guides also consume the worker's context budget on every run.
answers.version_caveat: Bundled skills such as /verify and /code-review cannot be preloaded as of v2.1.215, and no skill with disable-model-invocation: true can be. If the same definition is reused as an agent team teammate, the skills and mcpServers fields are not applied on that path, so the guarantee does not carry over to teammates.

answers.primary: A subagent with tools: Bash plus a PreToolUse hook in its frontmatter matching Bash, pointing at a validation script that inspects tool_input.command and exits 2 on INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE and friends. This is the documented db-reader shape: the system prompt tells the agent it is read-only and the hook is the deterministic backstop if it tries anyway.
answers.rejected_alternative: Bash permission deny rules in settings.json, rejected because deny patterns match command prefixes rather than SQL semantics and Claude Code explicitly refuses content-field rules such as Bash(command:...) as bypassable by compound commands.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. Exit code 2 from the PreToolUse hook blocks the call before it executes and feeds the stderr message back to the subagent, independently of anything the model decided.
answers.context_boundary: The hook process runs outside both context windows: it receives the tool call as JSON on stdin and returns only an exit code and a stderr line. The query output stays in the subagent's context, and only the report crosses back to the caller.
answers.lifecycle: Frontmatter hooks are installed when the subagent starts and torn down when it finishes, firing before every Bash call it makes in between. Session-wide hooks in settings.json also fire inside subagents, so a global guard would keep applying after this agent exits.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed at the moment of the check but the check itself is bypassable: a mutation hidden in a .sql file passed to the CLI, a heredoc, a wrapper script or a stored procedure never matches the regex. The dangerous direction is a hook that does not run at all, for example a non-executable script on macOS or Linux, or an untrusted project folder, which fails open silently.
answers.version_caveat: From v2.1.218 a project-level subagent's frontmatter hooks only run after you accept the workspace trust dialog for the folder containing the agent file; until then the agent still runs but the hook is skipped with only a debug-log error. Plugin subagents ignore the hooks field entirely, and on Windows the entry needs shell: powershell.

answers.primary: A skill that users invoke by name, carrying disallowed-tools: AskUserQuestion in its frontmatter (with disable-model-invocation: true so only a person can start it). That field removes the tool from Claude's available pool while the skill is active, and the doc names exactly this case, an autonomous background loop that should never ask.
answers.rejected_alternative: A permissions.deny rule for AskUserQuestion in settings.json, rejected because it is session-wide and permanent: it would silence every other turn in the session too, and it does not restore itself when the user speaks again.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness. Claude Code removes the tool from the pool for the duration, so the routine cannot call it even if the model decides it needs clarification.
answers.context_boundary: Everything runs in the invoking conversation's own context window; the skill's rendered content enters as a message and stays there for the rest of the session. Nothing is delegated, so no boundary is crossed and there is no summary to return.
answers.lifecycle: The restriction begins when the skill is invoked and clears automatically when the user sends their next message, which is precisely the requested restore behavior. Note the asymmetry: the instructions persist in context after the enforcement lapses, since Claude Code does not re-read the skill file on later turns.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for the tool but is advisory for the intent: with AskUserQuestion gone the model can still stall by asking in plain prose and waiting, which interrupts the user just as effectively without tripping any guard. The field also cannot remove EndConversation while other tools remain.
answers.version_caveat: No plan or experimental gate applies to disallowed-tools, but two adjacent details matter: disable-model-invocation: true also blocks the skill from being preloaded into subagents and, as of v2.1.196, from running when a scheduled task fires with it as the prompt. If the routine instead ran with context: fork, the point would be moot, since AskUserQuestion is stripped from every subagent regardless.

answers.primary: An agent team: the session becomes the lead and spawns five teammates, each a full independent Claude Code session with its own context window, that message each other by name over SendMessage and coordinate through the shared task list. This is the documented competing-hypotheses pattern, where the adversarial debate rather than the parallelism is the mechanism.
answers.rejected_alternative: Five parallel subagents, rejected on a structural ground rather than a stylistic one: subagents can only report back to the agent that spawned them and have no channel to each other, so they cannot disprove each other's theories.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness provides the mailboxes, the file-locked task claiming and the automatic message delivery; the model owns whether the debate actually converges and whether the surviving theory is right.
answers.context_boundary: Each teammate has its own fully independent context window and loads project context the way a normal session does, CLAUDE.md, MCP servers and skills, plus the lead's spawn prompt; the lead's conversation history does not carry over. What crosses between agents is messages, task-list entries and any shared findings doc they write.
answers.lifecycle: The team forms when the lead spawns the first teammate and lasts for the session: teammates stay running and addressable until they are asked to shut down or the session exits. The team config directory is removed at session end while the task list under ~/.claude/tasks persists for resumes, subject to cleanupPeriodDays.
answers.failure_mode: Token cost scales linearly with teammate count and is the main practical cost. Beyond that: task status lags when teammates forget to mark work complete and blocks dependents, the lead sometimes declares victory early or starts doing the work itself, every teammate permission prompt bubbles to the lead, and in-process teammates are not restored by /resume or /rewind.
answers.version_caveat: Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default: they require CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment, without which Claude will not spawn teammates at all. This behavior is described as of v2.1.178; teams cannot nest, there is one team per session, and split-pane display needs tmux or iTerm2 with it2.

answers.primary: Move the rule from the project rules file into a harness-enforced Read deny rule, permissions.deny with Read(vendor/**) (as a deny rule, that pattern also matches nested copies at any depth). The rules file is not the right owner here because the built-in Explore and Plan subagents are the two agents that skip CLAUDE.md, which is why delegated exploration keeps ignoring it while direct work obeys.
answers.rejected_alternative: Restating "ignore vendor/" in the delegation prompt each time, which is the documented workaround, rejected because it is advisory and per-call: it depends on Claude remembering to include it on every delegation, and the scenario says vendor must never be touched.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness, once the rule lives in permissions rather than CLAUDE.md. Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code and apply inside subagents; instructions in CLAUDE.md only shape what the model tries to do.
answers.context_boundary: The delegated searches run in the Explore or Plan subagent's own context window, which by design contains only its system prompt and the delegation message, not the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and not the parent conversation. A permission rule is evaluated by the harness at each tool call, so it does not need to cross that boundary to take effect.
answers.lifecycle: The deny rule applies from session start, to every tool call in the main conversation and in every subagent, for the whole session; it stops applying only if the settings file changes. There is no per-delegation step to remember.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for the built-in file tools but is best-effort beyond them: Read rules are applied to Grep and Glob on a best-effort basis, and they do not cover an arbitrary subprocess, so a ripgrep or a Python script launched through Bash can still walk vendor/. For OS-level enforcement across all processes you would need the sandbox instead.
answers.version_caveat: As of v2.1.208 a Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path, but not Write or NotebookEdit, so add an Edit deny rule if vendor must also be unwritable. If you would rather stop the delegation itself, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1 removes the built-in Explore and Plan agents so Claude explores directly under full CLAUDE.md context, and that requires v2.1.198 or later.
